abstract: The bird retina generates a dual acid load: aerobic metabolism in the outer retina produces CO2, while chronic anoxia in the inner retina yields lactic acid, raising the question of how intraocular pH homeostasis is maintained in birds. We show that chicken (Gallus gallus) vitreous pH remains close to blood pH despite these respiratory and metabolic acid-base challenges and a low non-bicarbonate buffering capacity, which is compensated by high vitreous bicarbonate. Spatial transcriptomics of eye tissue revealed enriched expression of carbonic anhydrase 2 and 4, and vacuolar-type H+-ATPase within the intraocular vascular structure, the pecten oculi. Immunohistochemistry confirmed the presence of carbonic anhydrase 2 in the pecten, suggesting an important role in ocular CO2 removal and pH regulation. Together, our findings demonstrate that bicarbonate buffering and pecten-mediated exchange of acid-base-relevant ions and metabolites act in concert to sustain retinal function under the extreme metabolic conditions of the bird eye.
